usage: general word for a road that cars drive on
examples: There are many cars on the road.
도로 + 로 to mark the route
nuance: 도로 is the everyday word for a road or street that vehicles use. It is bigger and more general than 골목 (alley). For a small neighborhood street you say 골목길, but for a main street you say 도로 or 큰길.
mistakes: Do not confuse 도로 (road) with 거리 (street); 도로 focuses on the driving surface for cars.
Do not say 도로에서 가요 for taking a route; use 도로로 가요.

usage: place where you put fuel in a car
put gas in at the gas station
가깝다 used to describe the station
examples: I put gas in at the gas station.
nuance: 주유소 is where drivers refuel a car, made of 주유 (fueling) plus 소 (place). Koreans often pair it with 기름을 넣다 (to put in gas). It is a place noun, so it usually takes 에 (to go to) or 에서 (action at the place).
mistakes: Do not say 가스 station; the Korean word is 주유소, even for gasoline.
Use 주유소에서 기름을 넣어요, not 주유소를 넣어요.

usage: an assigned or reserved seat on a vehicle
번호 = number printed on the ticket
examples: asking on a train or plane
Please give me a window seat.
nuance: 좌석 is the formal word for a seat on a bus, train, or plane, often one with a number. In casual speech people also say 자리, but 좌석 is what you see on tickets and signs. It is common in travel situations like reserving 좌석 on the KTX.
mistakes: 좌석 and 자리 both mean seat, but 좌석 is more formal and used for reserved transport seats.
Do not write 자석 (magnet); the correct spelling is 좌석.

usage: the place you are traveling to
examples: We almost arrived at the destination.
nuance: 목적지 means the destination, the place you are heading to on a trip. Taxi drivers and navigation apps use it a lot. It pairs with 도착하다 (to arrive) and takes 에 to mark the goal you reach.
mistakes: Use 목적지에 도착해요, not 목적지를 도착해요.
목적지 is the place you go to; do not confuse it with 출발지 (starting point).

usage: a street in town where people walk and shop
examples: There are many shops on the street.
nuance: 거리 means a street in a town, the kind you walk along past shops and cafes. It feels more like a public walking area than 도로, which stresses car traffic. Note 거리 also means distance, so context tells you which meaning is intended.
mistakes: 거리 can mean street or distance; the meaning depends on context.
For a big car road, prefer 도로; 거리 sounds like a walking street.

usage: where you wait for a train or subway
examples: I wait for the train on the platform.
The platform is full of people.
nuance: 승강장 is the platform where you wait to get on a train or subway. Station signs and announcements use 승강장 a lot. It is a place noun, so it takes 에서 for waiting and 으로 for moving toward it.
mistakes: Use 승강장에서 기다려요 (wait on the platform), not 승강장을 기다려요.
승강장 is the platform; do not confuse it with 정류장, which is a bus stop.

usage: the safety belt in a car or plane
examples: I always fasten the seatbelt in the car.
You may unfasten the seatbelt now.
nuance: 안전벨트 means seatbelt, made of 안전 (safety) plus 벨트 (belt). The verb you use is 매다 (to fasten) and 풀다 (to unfasten). You hear 안전벨트를 매세요 in taxis, buses, and airplanes.
mistakes: Use 안전벨트를 매다 (fasten the seatbelt), not 안전벨트를 입다.
To take it off, say 안전벨트를 풀다, not 안전벨트를 벗다.

usage: protective hat for riding a bike or motorcycle
examples: I wear a helmet when I ride a bike.
Be sure to wear a helmet.
The helmet is a bit small.
nuance: 헬멧 is a helmet, a loanword from English, worn for safety on bikes, motorcycles, and kickboards. The verb is 쓰다 (to put on the head) and 벗다 (to take off). It is essential vocabulary now that 전동킥보드 riding is common.
mistakes: Use 헬멧을 쓰다 (wear a helmet), not 헬멧을 입다, since it goes on the head.
To remove it, say 헬멧을 벗다, not 헬멧을 풀다.

usage: the station where your trip begins
get on at the departure station
examples: The departure station is Seoul Station.
I get on the train at the departure station.
nuance: 출발역 means the departure station, made of 출발 (departure) plus 역 (station). It is the station where your train trip starts. It naturally pairs with 도착역 (arrival station) and uses 에서 for getting on there.
mistakes: Use 출발역에서 타요 (get on at the departure station), not 출발역을 타요.
출발역 is where you start; do not confuse it with 도착역, where you get off.

usage: the station where your trip ends
get off at the arrival station
the next stop is the arrival station
examples: I get off at the arrival station.
The arrival station is Busan Station.
The next stop is the arrival station.
nuance: 도착역 means the arrival station, made of 도착 (arrival) plus 역 (station). It is the station where you get off at the end of your trip. It pairs with 내리다 (to get off) and uses 에서 to mark the place.
mistakes: Use 도착역에서 내려요 (get off at the arrival station), not 도착역을 내려요.
도착역 is where you get off; do not confuse it with 출발역, where you board.

examples: The plane ticket is too expensive.
I want to book a plane ticket.
nuance: 비행기표 means a plane ticket, made of 비행기 (airplane) plus 표 (ticket). You use it when buying or booking a flight. It pairs with 사다 (to buy) and 예약하다 (to reserve), like a train 표 but for flights.
mistakes: Use 비행기표를 사요 (buy a plane ticket), not 비행기표를 해요.
표 alone can mean any ticket; add 비행기 to specify a plane ticket.
